h1: The 4 Best Walk-Behind Leaf Blowers of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: four wheeled walk-behind leaf blowers compared on listed airflow, engine size and price for large lawns, lots and driveways.
summary: The Champion 212cc is the most clearly specified walk-behind here at 1200 CFM. The Yardmax matches that airflow for less, the SuperHandy is the established wheeled option in the middle, and the Landworks is a manually pushed jet sweeper.
intro: A walk-behind blower is a different tool from a handheld: you push it like a lawn mower, and it clears a whole row of leaves per pass. The mistake is expecting one to fit a small yard, since the wheels and engine are sized for open ground.

We ranked four walk-behind models on the airflow, engine size and fuel type their listings state, plus the price range each falls in. Backpack models in the same category are a different tool, so we left them out, and where listings are thin we flag it.

products.name: Champion Power Equipment 212cc 1200 CFM Walk-Behind Leaf Blower
products.verdict: The best-specified walk-behind here, with 212cc and 1200 CFM.
products.description:
The Champion lists a 212cc engine and 1200 CFM of airflow in a walk-behind format. It is the only pick in the $500+ range.

It leads because both its engine size and airflow are stated plainly, which is more than the others offer. Against the Yardmax, which lists the same 1200 CFM, you are paying for the engine detail and brand.

Buy it for large lots or driveways. The caveat is the price, which is the highest here.
products.idealFor: Large lots, driveways and heavy leaf fall.
products.skipIf: You have a small yard or tight budget.

products.name: Yardmax Gas Walk-Behind Blower
products.verdict: The same 1200 CFM as the Champion, in a lower price range.
products.description:
The Yardmax is a gas walk-behind blower listing 1200 CFM of airflow, in the $200 to $500 range.

Second place reflects that it matches the Champion's airflow at a lower price. What it lacks is a stated engine size in our data.

Best for homeowners with large lots who want the airflow without the top-end price. Check the engine size on the listing.
products.idealFor: Large lots on a smaller budget.
products.skipIf: You want the engine size confirmed.

products.name: SuperHandy Walk Behind Leaf Blower
products.verdict: A walk-behind from SuperHandy, sold under two listings, one noting gas.
products.description:
The SuperHandy is a walk-behind blower in the $200 to $500 range. A second listing under the same name notes gas power.

Third place reflects that no airflow figure appears in our data, so it cannot be compared with the 1200 CFM picks above.

Choose it if you prefer the brand. Confirm airflow and engine details on the listing first.
products.idealFor: Buyers who prefer the SuperHandy brand.

products.name: Landworks Leaf Blower Wheeled Walk Behind Jet Sweep Manual-Propelled
products.verdict: A wheeled, manually pushed gas jet sweeper.
products.description:
The Landworks is a wheeled gas walk-behind jet sweeper that you push by hand, in the $200 to $500 range.

Fourth place reflects that no airflow figure is listed in our data, which leaves it hardest to compare.

Best for open areas where you want to push a blower rather than carry one. Check airflow before ordering.
products.idealFor: Open areas where pushing beats carrying.

whatMatters.detail: CFM measures the volume of air moved. Walk-behind models start around 1200 CFM at the top end here. Check the figure in the title or bullets.
Engine size, measured in cc, indicates power. A 212cc engine is a typical lawn-equipment size. Look for it in the listing.
A manually pushed blower is lighter and simpler but takes effort on slopes. Check how the listing describes drive.
Walk-behind blowers take real garage space. Measure before buying.
Prices here run from $200 to $500 and up. Compare CFM and engine data before paying more.

faq.q: Is a walk-behind blower right for a small yard?
faq.a: Usually not. These are sized for open ground, and a handheld is easier on small yards.
Skipping airflow. Two of these four do not state CFM in our data.

faq.q: Is the Champion worth it over the Yardmax?
faq.a: Both list 1200 CFM. The Champion adds a stated 212cc engine but costs much more.
The Yardmax and Landworks are listed as gas. The SuperHandy has a gas listing as well.
Plan garage space. Walk-behind units are bulky compared with handhelds.
They are a different category from walk-behind models, so we left them out.

finalTake: The Champion is the clearest walk-behind pick, with 212cc and 1200 CFM listed. The Yardmax gives the same airflow for less. Check the missing specs on the SuperHandy and Landworks before you buy.
